paper.title: From private attitudes to public opinion: A dynamic theory of social impact

headline: Nowak-Szamrej-Latane 1990 Social Impact (agent-based): 1/3 locked clauses REPRO; mean minority fraction 0.045 (band [0.08,0.45]), bond 0.998, minority survival 0.10

verdicts.gate: P1 stable nonzero minority survives: mean final minority fraction in [0.08, 0.45] (not 0=consensus, not ~0.5=frozen noise)
reasons: mean final minority fraction = 0.0446 over 50 seeds (range [0.000, 0.488]); need in [0.08, 0.45]. 45/50 seeds reached full consensus (minority -> 0).

verdicts.gate: P2 spatial self-organisation: mean same-opinion bond fraction >= 0.75 at freeze (vs ~0.5 random)
P3 minority in coherent clusters: largest majority cluster >= 0.55*N AND a minority cluster >= 5 survives in >= 80% of seeds
reasons: mean largest-majority-cluster fraction = 0.9511 (need >= 0.55: OK); minority-cluster (>= 5) survival fraction = 0.1000 (5/50 seeds) (need >= 0.8: MISS)

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data. The contribution is whether the harness + locked-prediction discipline reproduce minority survival and spatial self-organisation under the EXACT locked functional (inverse-square decay, U[0,1] traits, deterministic h=0), and would honestly report a falsified clause

citations: Nowak, A., Szamrej, J. & Latane, B. (1990). From private attitudes to public opinion: A dynamic theory of social impact. Psychological Review 97(3):362-376. doi:10.1037/0033-295X.97.3.362.
Castellano, C., Fortunato, S. & Loreto, V. (2009). Statistical physics of social dynamics. Rev. Mod. Phys. 81:591-646 (impact functional, Eq. 16). doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.81.591.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the minority fraction, same-opinion bond fraction, and connected-cluster sizes
